version.changelog: Initial release: MTProto protocol layer, encryption, QuickAck, auth_key caching

llm.summary: The skill's documentation matches its stated purpose (MTProto handling and forwarding) but it describes sensitive operations (auth_key handling, AES-IGE decryption, forwarding plaintext payloads) while giving no provenance, no install steps, and no declaration of the credentials/config needed to contact the session service — these omissions and the sensitivity of the described actions warrant caution.

dimensions.detail: Name/description align with SKILL.md content: it documents MTProto handshake, AES-IGE decryption, payload extraction, QuickAck computation, and forwarding to a session service. The required capabilities described are coherent for implementing such a protocol layer.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions stay within the stated protocol scope and include concrete implementation notes (QuickAck, payload header layout, QueryAuthKey, gRPC forwarding). However, the instructions describe handling highly sensitive material (auth_key, decrypted plaintext) and network forwarding of decrypted payloads — this is expected for the purpose but increases risk and requires explicit operational controls that are not described.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec or code files — lowest install risk. No downloads or scripts are specified.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md implies the need for access to auth_key values and a session service (gRPC) to query/forward data, but the package declares no required environment variables, credentials, or config paths. That mismatch (sensitive runtime secrets implied but none declared) is notable and unexplained.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always-on inclusion and does not declare system-level persistence. Autonomous invocation is allowed by default (normal), but no additional privileges are requested.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill documents how to decrypt and forward MTProto messages, which necessarily involves handling auth_keys and plaintext user messages. Before installing or using it: 1) Confirm the skill's origin and perform a code review or request implementation/source — the package has no source or homepage. 2) Ask the author to declare required runtime credentials (auth_key storage, gRPC endpoint/credentials) and justify them. 3) Run any implementation in an isolated/test environment and audit network endpoints the skill uses to ensure messages aren't sent to unexpected destinations. 4) If you plan to deploy in production, insist on cryptographic-review (correct AES-IGE and QuickAck implementation) and strict key management; do not provide real keys until you verify the code and endpoints. If you need help evaluating a provided implementation, supply the code and I can highlight risky lines or missing checks.
